sections.html:
Mississippi's homestead exemption lowers the yearly property tax on your primary home. You have to apply for it, and the amount depends on which of three tiers you fit. The rules are in Mississippi Code Sections 27-33-1 through 27-33-79.

It affects the tax bill only. It does not change what the house is worth or what a buyer will pay. It matters at sale time because a lost or disallowed exemption can be charged back to you retroactively, and a buyer's lender may ask about the tax history.

sections.h2: Who qualifies and when to apply
sections.html:
Apply in person at the county Tax Assessor between January 1 and April 1. You must own the home and live in it as your primary residence on January 1. The assessor's office takes applications only during normal business hours, and a missed April 1 deadline means no exemption for that assessment year.

  • Ownership has to exist before January 1, and the ownership instrument must be filed with the Chancery Clerk before January 7.
  • You must meet the definition of head of family in Section 27-33-13 and hold title in a way Section 27-33-17 recognizes.
  • You and your spouse must be in compliance with Mississippi income tax law and the road and bridge privilege tax law.
  • Military personnel stationed outside Mississippi can qualify if they claim Mississippi residency and follow state law. A married servicemember needs both spouses to qualify.

sections.h2: What to bring to the assessor
sections.html:
Come with Social Security numbers or ITINs for every applicant, dates of birth, contact information, the property's physical address, the purchase price and down payment, a HUD closing statement or similar papers, and the tag numbers of all vehicles. A P.O. box cannot be used as the property address.

Tier 2 applicants add proof of age, such as a driver's license or birth certificate, or proof of total disability. Accepted disability proof includes a Social Security Act classification, a Railroad Retirement Act classification, a qualified retirement plan classification, IRS Schedule 3 and Schedule R, or a detailed letter from two physicians.

Mississippi homestead exemption tiers
TierWho it coversBenefit
Tier 1, regularQualified applicants under 65 who do not qualify for a disability tierTax credit of up to $300, based on property value
Tier 2, age or disabilityAt least 65 or totally disabled by January 1 of the filing yearExempt from tax on the first $7,500 of assessed value
Tier 3, totalService-connected totally disabled, honorably discharged former service members, anyone 90 or older, and certain unremarried surviving spousesExempt from all property taxes on the qualifying homestead

The Tier 2 benefit is also described as an exemption on the first $75,000 of true value. A single-family owner-occupied home is assessed at 10 percent, so $75,000 of true value equals $7,500 of assessed value. After the first year, the Tier 2 exemption can grow to include most later increases in value.

sections.h2: Do you have to reapply every year?
sections.html:
No. Once a valid application is on file, the credit repeats each year unless you lose the exemption or something changes after January 1 of the preceding year. These changes call for a new application:

  • A change in property description, ownership, use, or occupancy.
  • Marriage, divorce, remarriage, death, or a deed change.
  • A change in eligibility for disability or VA benefits.
  • Moving into a different tier, such as turning 65, which means reapplying in the next filing period.

When in doubt, call the county Tax Assessor before April 1. A late application cannot be fixed with a refund for that assessment year.

sections.h2: How you can lose the exemption
sections.html:
The exemption can be disallowed for any lapse in the underlying rules, and the cost can come back to you. Common reasons:

  • Not filing or not paying Mississippi income tax on time, or filing as a non-resident.
  • Failing to register vehicles properly. Vehicles must be tagged where they are domiciled, and that is the homestead property.
  • Claiming homestead on more than one property.
  • Not reapplying after a change in description, ownership, use, or occupancy.

A disallowance can require you to repay the tax jurisdictions for the exemption received in error. It can also affect future assessments, mortgage payments, and escrow payments, and can lead to collection efforts. Clear up any dispute before you list, since a buyer's lender may ask.

sections.h2: What happens to the exemption when you sell
sections.html:
It stays with the owner, not the house. A change in ownership requires a new application, so the buyer must apply during the next January 1 to April 1 window if they will live there.

Property is assessed to the owner of record on January 1, taxes are billed in November and December, and payment is due by February 1. If you sell mid-year, ask the closing agent how that year's taxes will be split.

A seller who moved out and rented the house should not expect to keep the exemption, since the applicant must live there on January 1. Real property that is not single-family owner-occupied is assessed at 15 percent instead of 10 percent. Tax status also shapes a cash sale. A buyer purchasing as-is will want to see that taxes are current, because unpaid balances can lead to the county tax sale and a two-year redemption period under Section 27-45-3.

1. Ask the Tax Assessor whether your exemption is active and which tier you are in.
  2. Confirm there is no disallowance or repayment demand on file.
  3. Pull the current tax bill from the Tax Collector and make sure it is paid.
  4. Tell the buyer, or the closing agent, that the new owner needs to file a fresh application in the next window.

Doing this early keeps surprises off the closing table, whether you sell on the open market or to a cash buyer.

faqs.q: When is the Mississippi homestead exemption deadline?
faqs.a: April 1. Applications are taken only at the county Tax Assessor between January 1 and April 1, and you must have owned and lived in the home on January 1.

faqs.q: How much is the homestead exemption in Mississippi?
faqs.a: It depends on the tier. Tier 1 gives a credit of up to $300, Tier 2 exempts the first $7,500 of assessed value for people 65 or older or totally disabled, and Tier 3 exempts all property tax for qualifying disabled former service members and certain surviving spouses.

faqs.q: Do I need to reapply for the homestead exemption every year?
faqs.a: No. Once approved, it carries forward unless ownership, use, occupancy, or the property description changes, or you qualify for a different tier.

faqs.q: Can I keep the exemption if I rent out my house?
faqs.a: The applicant must own and occupy the home as a primary residence on January 1. Call the county Tax Assessor before claiming it for a rented house, because a wrong claim can be disallowed.

faqs.q: Does the buyer get my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. A change in ownership requires a new application. The buyer must file with the county Tax Assessor during the next January 1 to April 1 window.
